sources.locator: "Afghan Civil War (1989–1992)", revision 1371765193, § lead and § Background (1978–1989)

explanation: The article defines this war by the end of the last one: it "took place between **the Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan on 15 February 1989 which ended the Soviet–Afghan War**, and 27 April 1992, the day after the proclamation of the Peshawar Accords proclaiming a new interim Afghan government". Its whole § Background (1978–1989) is the earlier war — the mujahideen revolt of October 1978, the 1979 Soviet invasion, nine years in which "between 500,000 and 2 million Afghans were killed and millions were displaced", and Gorbachev's announcement in 1987 of a withdrawal carried out between May 1988 and February 1989 — and the combatants of 1989 are the two sides that war left standing.
